# Contract: the token surface
<!-- Generated by /speckit.plan Phase 1 -->

The custom-property names components may rely on. This is the API of `@fablab/ui`: adding a
token is additive, **renaming or removing one is a breaking change** for every consumer.

## The rule that matters most

**Exactly one colour token is per-organization.**

| Token | Value | Who sets it |
|---|---|---|
| `--color-primary` | `theme.primaryColor`, defaulting to `--color-rosa` | **Per organization** (CLR-001) |
| `--color-navy` `--color-azul` `--color-teal` `--color-amarelo` `--color-laranja` `--color-rosa` `--color-claro` | fixed hexes | Platform — identical for every organization |

> **`--color-rosa` is not the accent; `--color-primary` is.** A CTA styled with
> `--color-rosa` renders identically for the CITe organization and therefore passes every
> test — and silently fails to co-brand for the second one. This is the single most likely
> way feature 001 breaks feature 007, so components use `--color-primary` for anything that
> means *"this organization's accent"*, and `--color-rosa` only where the literal Fab Lab
> pink is intended regardless of tenant.

## Colour

```css
--color-navy    /* #191C37  base background, text on light */
--color-azul    /* #3760AA  links, icons, graphic elements  */
--color-teal    /* #74B7A5  hero band, progress detail, status chips */
--color-amarelo /* #F8C810  XP, rewards, mission icons, numbering */
--color-laranja /* #EE703E  the canonical logo chip */
--color-rosa    /* #EE9DC4  Fab Lab pink — default for --color-primary */
--color-claro   /* #DCE7E3  light surfaces, text on dark */
--color-primary /* per-organization accent: CTAs, active tabs, card titles */
```

Backgrounds are named by role rather than colour, so the white-background pages
(`docs/product/visual-identity.md` § Paleta) do not need per-page overrides:

```css
--surface-page      /* navy by default */
--surface-card
--surface-inverted  /* the white content area used by Biblioteca 3D and Aulas */
--text-on-dark  --text-on-light
```

## Typography

```css
--font-display  /* Aldo the Apache → condensed sans fallback */
--font-logotype /* SquareFont     → condensed sans fallback (NOT in repo — CLR-002) */
--font-body     /* Comfortaa      → system-ui, sans-serif   */
--text-xs … --text-3xl
```

Every face declares `font-display: swap` and a real fallback stack. `--font-logotype` **must
look acceptable in fallback**, because CI and any deployment without the licensed file will
always render it that way (SC-012).

## Layout

```css
--bp-mobile   /* 390  */
--bp-tablet   /* 834  */
--bp-desktop  /* 1440 */
--space-1 … --space-12   --radius-sm --radius-md   --shadow-hard
```

Breakpoints are tokens so a media query never contains a bare number — the three values are
*design targets* from the mockups, not arbitrary thresholds, and naming them keeps that
traceable.

## Documented contrast pairs

`tokens/index.ts` exports `DOCUMENTED_PAIRS`, and `contrast.test.ts` iterates it (SC-006).
**A pair that fails WCAG AA cannot be documented** — which is the mechanism that finally
answers the open question in `visual-identity.md` § Paleta about pink-on-navy small text.

## What `@fablab/ui` may never import

Inherited from feature 000 and extended (FR-018): no `payload`, no `@payloadcms/*`, no Next
*server* APIs, no IO. The package receives resolved values as props or custom properties.
Its React dependency is a **peer** — the app owns the React instance.
